scope: The ten Table 4 mixtures used for preliminary compression testing (composition in % of the mixture) and the Table 7 mean compressive strengths of 2 n and 3 n. Printed/cast results for geopolymers A and B (Figures 7–11, Table 8) are not mapped to these labels in the paper and are not transcribed.

materials.name: Bark boiler ash
materials.detail: Bark ash, which is a by-product of the paper and pulp industry, is used as the primary binder ingredient instead of fly ash.

materials.name: C&D waste
materials.detail: The C&D waste was employed as a filler and reactive material in this investigation

materials.name: Metakaolin
materials.detail: Commercial metakaolin (having 47% of Al and Si in a 1:2 ratio) was used as a reactive pozzolan and source of Al and Si.

materials.name: sodium silicate solution
materials.detail: For the alkaline reagent, a sodium silicate solution having a molar ratio of 2.4–2.6 was used (31% SiO2 and 13% Na2O).

materials.name: Sand c
materials.detail: Sand (coarse and fine) was received as the leftover product from mine tailings and used as a filler material with no reactive components.

materials.name: Sand F
materials.detail: Sand (coarse and fine) was received as the leftover product from mine tailings and used as a filler material with no reactive components.

gaps: Table 4 is headed "Mixture composition (%)"; rows do not all sum to 100 (e.g. 5 p sums to 96), so the basis is recorded as % of total mix as printed. The Al, Si and "Curing Min" columns are not ingredient amounts and are not transcribed.
Table 3 water-to-silicate and silicate-to-binder entries are ranges or single descriptors that conflict with Table 4; not transcribed (the review-note conflict stays).
Strength of the other eight mixtures is only in Figure 6; geopolymers A and B (setting, shape stability, 7/28-day cast and extruded strengths, Table 8 densities) are not linked to a Table 4 label.
Table 7 lists ten single-specimen values per material; only the stated mean is transcribed.
